alt: The Law Commission has a chair who is a High Court or Court of Appeal judge, four other commissioners drawn from judges, practising lawyers and legal academics, and support from research lawyers and parliamentary draftsmen. Its section 3 duty covers codification, eliminating anomalies, repealing obsolete enactments, reducing separate enactments, simplification and modernisation.
caption: A judge-led body of five commissioners with a duty to keep the whole law under review.

alt: Five steps of a Law Commission project: choosing the work through programmes or references, research and scoping, a consultation paper, a final report usually with a draft Bill, and the government response and implementation. Three later changes target implementation: the Law Commission Act 2009 annual report, the 2010 protocol and a House of Lords special procedure.
caption: The Commission researches, consults and drafts; implementation rests with government and Parliament.

alt: Four functions in a grid. Reform changes the law to improve it, as in the Fraud Act 2006. Codification gathers statute and case law on a topic into one code; the draft Criminal Code of 1989 was never enacted. Consolidation combines several Acts into one without changing substance, as in the Sentencing Act 2020. Repeal removes obsolete laws through Statute Law (Repeals) Bills.
caption: Reform changes the law; codification, consolidation and repeal reorganise and tidy it.

alt: A timeline of Acts based on Law Commission work: Computer Misuse Act 1990, Law Reform (Year and a Day Rule) Act 1996, Contracts (Rights of Third Parties) Act 1999, Fraud Act 2006, Coroners and Justice Act 2009 (partly implementing the 2006 homicide report), Electronic Trade Documents Act 2023 and Automated Vehicles Act 2024.
caption: Commission reports lie behind Acts across criminal, contract and commercial law.

alt: Codification combines Acts and case law on a topic into one code; consolidation combines several Acts into one Act without changing their substance. Codification has largely been abandoned: the 1989 draft Criminal Code and the Offences Against the Person reports were not implemented. Consolidation continues, as with the Sentencing Act 2020, using a fast-track procedure.
caption: Codification takes in case law and changes the shape of the law; consolidation only gathers statutes.

alt: Two columns. Advantages: independence, expertise, wide consultation, draft Bills, whole-area review, technical areas and a clearer statute book. Disadvantages: no power to implement, delay and partial implementation, political reluctance, failed codification, and selection of work depending on government support. The balancing point notes that reforms since 2009 have reduced but not removed the implementation problem.
caption: Quality of work is high; the weak link is getting reports enacted.
